frozen_original.title: DOGE accesses private IRS tax records of 150 million Americans
frozen_original.synopsis: DOGE operatives gained unauthorized access to IRS systems containing private tax records of approximately 150 million Americans, in one of the largest privacy breaches of government data in US history. The access granted DOGE personnel the ability to view complete tax returns, financial data, and confidential taxpayer information for virtually every American adult. IRS employees who attempted to block the access were threatened with termination, and the agency's inspector general launched an emergency investigation into the breach.

current_description_proposal.description_medium: In February and March 2025, DOGE representatives sought broad access to IRS systems containing highly sensitive taxpayer information and proposed using tax records to check federal benefit programs. Reporting on February 20 said Treasury agreed to restrict DOGE to anonymized data rather than personal taxpayer records. The evidence therefore does not support the stored claim that DOGE actually obtained complete tax records of approximately 150 million Americans.
current_description_proposal.description_long: In February 2025, representatives of the Department of Government Efficiency sought broad access to sensitive Internal Revenue Service systems and proposed using tax records to check federal benefit programs. Treasury agreed to restrict DOGE to anonymized information rather than personal taxpayer records. Later reporting described continued efforts to expand access, while IRS lawyers raised privacy concerns about comparing benefits and tax data. The distinction between a request, access to anonymized information, and viewing identifiable returns matters because tax records contain highly sensitive personal details. The reporting supports a broad access request and a limited arrangement; it does not support the claim that DOGE obtained complete tax files for about 150 million Americans. The episode raised questions about how government efficiency projects can use personal data and what safeguards should apply when agencies share records. It documents an effort to gain access, not a mass transfer of identifiable taxpayer files.
